gloss: gift brought when visiting; host gift

definitions.gloss: a gift brought when visiting someone's home; a host gift
definitions.explanation: a present that one brings when visiting someone, as a gesture of politeness and gratitude

examples.japanese: {手土産|てみやげ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{和菓子|わがし}→和菓子：04962_wagashi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}った→買う：00489_kau⟧。
examples.english: I bought Japanese sweets as a host gift.

examples.japanese: ⟦{友人|ゆうじん}→友人：03649_yuujin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{家|いえ}→家：00612_ie⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{手土産|てみやげ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{持|も}って→持つ：00478_motsu⟧いった。
examples.english: I brought a gift when I visited my friend's house.

examples.japanese: ⟦{取引先|とりひきさき}→取引先：11083_torihikisaki⟧⟦へ→へ：02473_he⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{挨拶|あいさつ}→挨拶：02505_aisatsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{手土産|てみやげ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{忘|わす}れ→忘れる：00474_wasureru⟧ず⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧。
examples.english: Don't forget to bring a gift when greeting our business partner.

notes:
FORMS:
⟦{手|て}→手：00569_te⟧ (hand) + ⟦{土産|みやげ}→土産：03746_miyage⟧ (souvenir) → something brought by hand

DIFFERENCE FROM お{土産|みやげ}:
- ⟦お{土産|みやげ}→お土産：01353_omiyage⟧: souvenirs from a trip
- {手土産|てみやげ}: gifts brought when visiting someone

COMMON {手土産|てみやげ} ITEMS:
- ⟦{和菓子|わがし}→和菓子：04962_wagashi⟧ (Japanese sweets)
- ⟦{洋菓子|ようがし}→洋菓子：04998_yougashi⟧ (Western sweets)
- ⟦{果物|くだもの}→果物：00509_kudamono⟧ (fruit)
- ⟦お{酒|さけ}→お酒：01045_osake⟧ (alcohol)
- ⟦{地元|じもと}→地元：09941_jimoto⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{名産品|めいさんひん} (local specialties)

ETIQUETTE:
- Choose items that can be shared
- Consider the recipient's tastes and dietary restrictions
- Avoid items with odd numbers (except ⟦{五|ご}→五：00697_go⟧ and {七|しち})
- Present with both hands, saying 「⟦つまらないものですが→つまらないものですが：23570_tsumaranaimonodesuga⟧」

BUSINESS CONTEXT:
{手土産|てみやげ} is especially important in business settings (⟦{取引先|とりひきさき}→取引先：11083_torihikisaki⟧⟦へ→へ：02473_he⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{挨拶|あいさつ}→挨拶：02505_aisatsu⟧) and shows respect and consideration.
